note: NEW 2026 hypothesis (round 6), pre-registered before any bet: when our AI news reader learns that a regular WR/TE/RB is out, the books are slow to raise his teammates' props, so the next men up are worth an OVER before the market adjusts. The 2023-25 props studies only used the official injury report and found the closing prop line efficient; this tests the window between the news and the books. Paper only. Do not edit to fit results; bump version instead.

trigger.regular: player's average offensive snap share over his team's last 3 games this season >= 50% (nflverse snap counts)

beneficiaries: same team and same position (WR->WR, TE->TE, RB->RB), average snap share over the last 3 games between 15% and 85%, not themselves reported out; the top 2 by snap share
bet: OVER on each beneficiary x market at the allowed books (my_books.json): lowest point first, then best price; main line only (both prices within -200..+170); 1 unit; one bet per beneficiary-market-game

grading.close: our props fetch of the same event and markets 10-90 min before kickoff (fetched only for games with open bets)
grading.clv: price x median no-vig P(over) among close books quoting the SAME point - 1; also points_moved = median close point (all books) - our point (positive = the market raised the line after we bet)
grading.result: nflverse weekly player stats vs the point; no offensive snap = void

cost: Odds API event call, 2 markets x regions=us = 2 credits per trigger, plus 2 at the close for games with open bets (~15 triggers/week ~ 60 credits/week)
